long_biography.plain_text:
Swiss entrepreneur Ernesto Bertarelli founded Alinghi in 2000 to mount a challenge for the America's Cup. He sailed aboard the team as it won on its first attempt in 2003, returning the trophy to Europe after more than a century. Four years later, as afterguard runner and grinder, he joined the successful defence in Valencia.

After a former pharmaceutical headquarters in Geneva was placed on the market, Bertarelli joined a consortium that acquired the site and created Campus Biotech. The centre now houses neuroscience and neuroengineering research. Through the Bertarelli Foundation, he and his sister Dona support marine science, life-science research and local communities.
long_biography.html:
Swiss entrepreneur Ernesto Bertarelli founded Alinghi in 2000 to mount a challenge for the America's Cup. He sailed aboard the team as it won on its first attempt in 2003, returning the trophy to Europe after more than a century. Four years later, as afterguard runner and grinder, he joined the successful defence in Valencia.

After a former pharmaceutical headquarters in Geneva was placed on the market, Bertarelli joined a consortium that acquired the site and created Campus Biotech. The centre now houses neuroscience and neuroengineering research. Through the Bertarelli Foundation, he and his sister Dona support marine science, life-science research and local communities.

uncertainties.detail: The source record gives the United Kingdom, while the current Forbes profile places Bertarelli in Gstaad and his official B-Flexion biography says he lives in Switzerland. A correction to Switzerland is proposed for review.

The existing Wikipedia article gives the full-name form Ernesto Silvio Maurizio Bertarelli, but no sufficiently strong independent source reviewed here confirms both middle names. The field remains unproposed.

Italian birth and background do not establish present Italian citizenship. A 2002 direct quotation states that Bertarelli did not then hold an Italian passport, so no secondary nationality is proposed.

Forbes describes the Serono stake as inherited, but also documents substantial expansion under Bertarelli and his sister. Because he was already chief executive and official histories show a biotechnology shift and more than tripled revenue, Inherited and expanded is used rather than simply Inherited.

B-Flexion is privately held and does not publish complete segment valuations. Finance & Investments is selected because the current platform principally seeds, acquires and builds asset managers across several investment classes while also holding operating healthcare businesses.

Bertarelli is B-Flexion's chairman, but public material does not detail every day-to-day investment decision. Family office principal reflects his leadership of the family investment platform without assigning the operating work of its specialist managers to him.

Focused searches found no identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok or personal website. B-Flexion, Alinghi, the Bertarelli Foundation and family pages are organisational rather than personal accounts and are not substituted.
The stored Wikipedia URL is an exact-person match and remains unchanged. Its claims are used only as orientation or where corroborated by stronger first-party sources.

Alinghi is included because Bertarelli founded the racing team, sailed in defined crew roles and won the America's Cup twice. This is an independently documented competitive career, not an inference from private vessel ownership.
Vava II and Vava were used only to disambiguate the source owner record. Neither biography nor any wealth classification mentions or depends on those vessels.
